what: the public SVG surface — the version x variant dispatch and its seam checks
note: `test: null` — the whole suite. The point of this ticket's mutations is that
the *dispatch* is the only new mechanism: every builder underneath it was
already proved by its own parity file, so a mutation here has to be killed by
the new sweep and not by a sibling. Narrowing the run would hide which.
Group A is the dispatch itself — what upstream's avatar.js decides. Group B
is the public seam's own promises: the arguments that have no default, the
type check the scene model can only assert, and what the barrel exports.
The six `size is hardcoded` cases are the run that found a real hole rather
than confirming a guard. The main 600-render matrix renders at 80, so `size:
80` reproduces it exactly on every arm — and `sizePassthrough` held `marble`
alone from #33 to #59, so five of the six survived the entire suite. The
fixture now carries every variant at both sizes and all six die. Keep all six:
one per arm is the only shape that can catch the next one.
`the default variant is beam` caught the run's first survivor, and the fix was
a deletion rather than a test: `buildAvatarScene` carried its own
`variant`/`square` defaults, which its only caller always overrides. Both are
now required, and the case targets the public function's default — the one a
caller can actually reach.
Group C is the #59 completeness pass's harvest — every one of these SURVIVED
the 14-case run and the whole 677-test suite. Two lenses predicted all of
them green and all nine were. They are kept because each names a distinct
way for the dispatch to drop an argument that nothing else was watching.
Two mutations were harvested and then **dropped**, because each survives by
design rather than by neglect — and a case that cannot die would make the
runner's non-zero exit meaningless:
* `export 'scene/scene.dart';` inside version.dart. It leaked the whole
scene model onto the barrel before #59's completeness pass; with a `show`
on every barrel export it is inert. Measured both ways: with the show,
`SvgNode` is an undefined class at the barrel; without it, it resolves.
What guards the property is `a barrel export loses its show clause`.
* `for (final v in values.reversed)`. A single scan over unique keys is
order-independent, so no order is observable — which is exactly why the
ordering test that used to sit in api_surface_test.dart could not fail.
What guards it is uniqueness, so `two variants claim the same upstream
name` is the case that replaced it.
